frequency_question: How often do structural frictions (conciliation mechanisms, essential services maintenance acts, court injunctions, and employer settlements) successfully prevent a called indefinite strike from commencing within the final five-day countdown?
membership_rule: Includes all instances where a major multi-employer union federation officially announced or threatened an indefinite strike date, with a remaining window of five days or fewer before initiation, where conciliation or structural barriers were actively engaged. Excludes localized single-firm strikes or strikes without formal national federation backing.

cases.name: Public Sector Undertaking Bank Strike Call (Nov 2007)
All India Bank Employees Association Strike Call (Aug 2009)

coverage_note: 8 named historical final-window countdowns representing major national federation strike calls involving systemic conciliation intervention.
known_gaps: Some localized or unrecorded conciliation settlements at the last minute prior to 2010 may be undercounted.
skeleton: Decomposed into national federation strike countdowns over the last 20 years that reached the final 5-day window, tracked against whether conciliation/structural friction successfully averted the stoppage.
validity_reason: Labor laws, conciliation frameworks, and union-management negotiation structures in the jurisdiction evolve slowly over decades.
